texts.preamble: Makkhan Kushwaha vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 24 February, 2020 Author: Jagdish Prasad Gupta Bench: Jagdish Prasad Gupta 1 Cr.Rev.No.629/2020 High Court Of Madhya Pradesh Cr.Rev.No.629/2020 Jabalpur : 24/02/2020 Shri D.K.Trivedi, Advocate for the applicant. Shri Abhinav Dubey, G.A. for the respondent / State. Record of both the courts below have been received.
texts.facts: However, at the outset learned counsel for the applicant prays for withdrawal of I.A.No.2238/2020 and prays that this revision may kindly be heard finally as the applicant has completed 25 days in jail custody and he does not want to press this revision on merits and only wants to argue on the point of sentence. Facts, as emerged from the findings of both the courts below and giving rise to the present revision, briefly stated, are that on 13.5.2009 at about 8 AM near Adhartal Police Station, Jabalpur, the applicant accused was found carrying milk in an auto and on being stopped and on enquiry by the local Health officer, he was found selling milk without licence of food item milk under the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act. The sample was collected by the Health Officer, which was found adulterated. The offence was registered against the applicant and complaint case was filed before the trial court. Being aggrieved therewith, this revision has been filed.
texts.arguments: Learned counsel for the applicant submitted that the findings of both the courts below are contrary to law. Statements of the witnesses are not reliable. The applicant is a first offender and under the aforesaid provision, there is no minimum sentence. The applicant is facing trial since 2009 and he is in custody since 30.1.2020. The applicant is not a habitual criminal. If he is kept in custody for a long time he will come in the contact of hardcore criminals and there will be no possibility of the applicant to reform himself and no purpose will be served as he got sufficient lesson. In such circumstances, the ends of justice would be met if the applicant is sentenced to the period already undergone by him. Learned Govt. Advocate appearing for the State has contended that the finding of conviction is based on legal evidence.
texts.petitioner_arguments: Learned counsel for the applicant submitted that the findings of both the courts below are contrary to law. Statements of the witnesses are not reliable.
